dmm-2010-power-01.title: Use the definition twice
dmm-2010-power-01.body: By definition, $P(B\mid A)=\dfrac{P(A\text{ and }B)}{P(A)}$, so $P(A\text{ and }B)=P(B\mid A)\,P(A)$. Then $P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\text{ and }B)}{P(B)}=\dfrac{P(B\mid A)\,P(A)}{P(B)}$. ∎

dmm-2010-power-02.title: Expand with the definition
dmm-2010-power-02.body: $P(A\text{ and }B\mid C)=\dfrac{P(A\text{ and }B\text{ and }C)}{P(C)}=\dfrac{P(B\text{ and }C)}{P(C)}\cdot\dfrac{P(A\text{ and }B\text{ and }C)}{P(B\text{ and }C)}=P(B\mid C)\cdot P(A\mid B\text{ and }C).$ ∎
